title: Bounded Git push with protected credential references
objective: Introduce the second destination-scoped Git network capability: an approved git.push operation that pushes one explicit local source ref to one explicit remote destination ref on one workspace-bound canonical HTTPS destination after fresh local approval, with expected remote-ref protection, non-fast-forward rejection, hard force-push denial, destination revalidation, resulting remote-ref verification, and a protected credential-reference architecture that never exposes raw secrets. git.fetch.preview and approved git.fetch remain unchanged; generic network, shell, push-bypass, and ambient-credential authority must not be introduced.

include: workspace policy records for explicitly configured Git push destinations identified by stable policy ids rather than caller-supplied arbitrary URLs
canonical destination validation requiring https, an explicit DNS hostname, port 443 or the implicit HTTPS default, no URL userinfo, no query, no fragment, and no alternate Git transport syntax
explicit local source ref restricted to refs/heads/<branch> short-branch form and explicit remote destination ref restricted to refs/heads/<branch> short-branch form
expected local HEAD binding plus expected prior remote-ref state obtained from a local-only read-only stale-protection preview with no DNS and no network

DNS resolution through a testable resolver boundary followed by public-address classification that rejects loopback, private, link-local, multicast, unspecified, documentation/special-use, and otherwise non-public destinations
binding one validated destination address to the actual Git HTTPS request so DNS rebinding cannot silently widen the approved destination

fresh local approval for every push, bound to workspace, repository identity, policy revision, destination policy id, canonical HTTPS URL, hostname, port, pinned destination address, source ref, destination ref, expected HEAD, expected prior remote-ref state, and credential-reference identifier without raw secret material
post-approval re-resolution and policy revalidation before network use; any material policy, repository, HEAD, destination, credential-binding, or ref drift fails closed
non-fast-forward rejection and hard force-push denial with no force, delete, or wildcard refspec path

fixed Git transport hardening including HTTPS-only protocol allowlisting, disabled redirects, TLS verification enabled, no proxy inheritance, no cookies, no extra HTTP headers inherited from repository policy, no askpass/interactive prompt, no submodule recursion, no tags, and no prune

protected credential-reference architecture with explicit credential capability binding, secret redaction in tool output, logs, audit, command evidence, and child process environment, and no ambient Git credential-manager inheritance

repository-local configuration inspection that rejects URL rewrite rules, credential-helper overrides, or other local Git configuration capable of redirecting, authenticating, or widening the approved push destination

postcondition verification that checked-out HEAD, branch, index/worktree material state remain unchanged except for the intended remote-tracking evidence update and only the authorized destination ref is written remotely

typed evidence reporting canonical destination identity, approved/pinned address, source ref, destination ref, prior remote-ref state, resulting remote-ref object id, credential-reference identifier with redacted secret material, and unchanged local HEAD evidence

deterministic unit/security tests with injected DNS results plus at least one no-cost real HTTPS push qualification against an explicitly pinned public test source or an explicitly credentialless test destination where no-cost push is unavailable, with the unavailable path explicitly recorded as unproven rather than mocked
Windows and Ubuntu exact-head qualification with SG-000015 local mutation and SG-000016 fetch regressions retained
exclude: wildcard, negative, tag, notes, replace, or caller-selected arbitrary destination refspecs
credential helpers, askpass, interactive username/password/token prompts except through the protected credential-reference path
SSH, git://, file://, ext, remote helpers, SCP-style syntax, or arbitrary protocols
private, loopback, link-local, multicast, unspecified, metadata-style, or other non-public destination addresses
checkout, merge, reset, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, stash, clean, or worktree mutation caused by push
general network.fetch or generic HTTP client authority
raw shell, cmd.exe, or PowerShell authority
approval bypass or persistent approval reuse

authority_delta.filesystem: Approved git.push may update the configured remote destination ref and local remote-tracking evidence inside an already trusted repository; checked-out HEAD, current branch, index, worktree, tags, and arbitrary refs are not writable through this grain.
authority_delta.process: No generic process authority. The typed Git provider may execute only fixed read/state commands and the fixed hardened HTTPS push command required by this grain.
authority_delta.network: Approved git.push adds DIRECT_DESTINATION egress only for an explicitly configured HTTPS Git destination whose hostname and port are policy-bound and whose validated public address is pinned to the actual request. No generic socket/HTTP/proxy authority is added.
authority_delta.secrets: Credential references only. Raw secrets never appear in request arguments, tool output, logs, audit, command argv, persisted Git config, unrelated child environments, or CI output. Ambient credential helpers and managers are denied.
authority_delta.approval: Fresh local approval is mandatory for every push and binds exact destination, pinned address, repository/ref state, credential-reference identifier, and policy revision. Preview requires no approval because it is local/read-only and performs no DNS/network activity.

invariants: No caller can turn git.push into arbitrary network access because the URL originates from workspace policy rather than request data
Only canonical HTTPS destinations on the approved hostname and port are usable; alternate Git protocols and redirect widening fail closed
The address actually used by Git is one public address validated and bound by Cotra rather than an unverified later DNS result

Repository-local URL rewrite, proxy, credential, header, cookie, or transport configuration cannot widen, authenticate, or decorate the approved request outside the protected credential-reference path
Every push requires exact expected local HEAD and exact prior remote-ref state before and after approval
Push writes only the approved destination ref and never force-updates, deletes, or widens refs
Force push remains impossible; no force transport flag or delete refspec is exposed
Raw credentials never appear in request/tool output, logs, audit, command argv, persisted Git config, or unrelated child environments
No ambient Git credential manager or caller-supplied raw token is promoted into authority
Existing SG-000015 local branch/stage/unstage/commit controls and SG-000016 fetch preview/fetch controls remain unchanged
Public process.spawn remains restricted to the SG-000010-qualified System32 whoami.exe target and public powershell.run remains absent
No browser/UI, elevation, generic network, or approval bypass authority is introduced

acceptance.claim: Tests prove workspace Git push destination policy accepts only canonical HTTPS hostname destinations and rejects URL userinfo, query/fragment, non-443 explicit ports, HTTP, SSH/SCP, git://, file://, ext/remote-helper forms, malformed hostnames, caller-provided arbitrary URLs, and duplicate/ambiguous policy ids.

Exact-head tests prove the push stale-protection preview is local-only/read-only: it performs no DNS/network call or approval request, returns exact current HEAD plus deterministic source and destination refs and current remote-ref object id/ABSENT value, and leaves refs/index/worktree/object state unchanged.

Resolver/policy tests prove loopback, private, link-local, multicast, unspecified, documentation/special-use, and other non-public IPv4/IPv6 results fail before approval/network use; approved public resolution is pinned into the actual Git HTTP transport configuration and post-approval resolution/policy drift fails closed.

Exact-head tests prove approved git.push accepts only one validated refs/heads/<branch> source and one validated refs/heads/<branch> destination with exact expected HEAD and exact expected prior remote-ref state, rejects non-fast-forward updates, and hard-denies force, delete, and wildcard refspecs.

Network command-plan tests prove HTTPS is the only allowed Git protocol; redirects are disabled; TLS verification is enabled; proxy, cookies, extra headers, askpass/interactive prompts, tags, prune, submodules, arbitrary refspecs, URL rewrites, and inherited secret-like environment cannot widen the operation outside the protected credential-reference path.

Credential tests prove raw secrets never appear in request arguments, tool output, logs, audit, command argv, persisted Git config, unrelated child environments, or CI output; ambient credential helpers and managers are denied; only explicit credential references are bound.

Exact-head tests prove approval denial/unavailability, stale HEAD/ref/policy/destination/credential-binding state, unsafe repository-local Git configuration, DNS-address widening, transport error, or postcondition mismatch fail closed and do not mutate checked-out HEAD/index/worktree or unauthorized refs.

Successful push evidence verifies the resulting remote destination ref object id and proves checked-out HEAD, current branch, index/worktree material state are unchanged except for intended remote-tracking evidence. A no-cost real HTTPS qualification exercises the actual hardened transport against an explicitly pinned public source or records the push path as unproven where no no-cost destination exists.
Tests prove force push, branch deletion, raw credential access, arbitrary Git/network commands, general network.fetch, public PowerShell, and broader process authority remain unreachable.
SG-000015 branch/stage/unstage/commit, SG-000016 fetch preview/fetch, and read-only git.status/diff/log regressions remain green with no authority expansion outside the bounded push surface.

Exact-head Windows/Ubuntu Rust, Node, Governance, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, exact-diff security review, manual review of excluded security-sensitive files, and zero unresolved blocking review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.p06_exit: After this push grain closes with canonical evidence, COTRA-P06 exits only when branch, stage, unstage, commit, fetch, and push are all canonically closed with force push denied by default, network policy applied, and resulting refs verified.
successor_requirements.credential_policy: No ambient Git credential manager or caller-supplied raw token may be promoted into authority by implication in any successor. Any authenticated successor must bind secrets through an explicit protected credential capability and must prove that raw credentials never appear in request/tool output, logs, audit, command argv, persisted Git config, or unrelated child environments.

done_when: Bounded approved git.push is merged and post-merge verified with explicit workspace destination policy, short source and destination branch validation, public-address classification and request pinning, redirect/proxy/credential suppression outside the protected credential-reference path, exact approval/state binding, non-fast-forward rejection with hard force-push denial, resulting remote-ref evidence, real no-cost HTTPS qualification or explicit unproven record, and no ambient credential or generic network authority.
